pr.body:
We're adding one more step in the GitHub integration installation pipeline, namely GitHub OAuth2 authorize. This is transparent from the UX perspective as the data exchange happens without user interaction.

The pipeline will now fail in these cases:
- If there is a mismatch between currently authenticated GitHub user (derived from OAuth2 authorize step) and the user who installed the GitHub app (https://github.com/apps/sentry-io)
- If there is a mismatch between `state` parameter supplied by user and pipeline signature
- If GitHub could not generate correct `access_token` from the `code` (wrong or attempt of re-use of `code`).

In all those cases, this error is shown:
![image](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/assets/1127549/18923861-2ead-4cf5-adda-7738aef801d7)
pr.title: fix(security): validate GitHub user during integration installation

raw_findings.body: The pipeline proceeds to finish the installation without comparing users, creates or links an integration without installer metadata, and defeats the new identity validation.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The validation is only applied to a race-dependent subset of installations, allowing an unverified OAuth account to complete setup.
raw_findings.impact: The pipeline proceeds to finish the installation without comparing users, creates or links an integration without installer metadata, and defeats the new identity validation.
raw_findings.root_cause: The no-Integration branch advances directly instead of enforcing the installer identity check required by the new flow.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Do not advance when the integration or its installer metadata is absent; wait for or explicitly fail the installation until an active GitHub integration with a verified sender is available.
raw_findings.title: Missing integration lets the OAuth user bypass installer validation
raw_findings.trigger: The GitHub installation webhook has not created an Integration before the OAuth callback reaches GitHubInstallation, while the authenticated GitHub user differs from the user who installed the app.

raw_findings.body: The exception escapes OAuthLoginView and the user receives a server error rather than the installation failure dialog.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Transient OAuth-provider failures terminate the web request instead of following the pipeline's error path.
raw_findings.impact: The exception escapes OAuthLoginView and the user receives a server error rather than the installation failure dialog.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new synchronous token exchange is performed outside any exception handler.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the token exchange in the established OAuth callback exception handling and convert transport and upstream failures into the error response.

raw_findings.trigger: The GitHub OAuth token endpoint is unreachable or raises an SSL/connection exception while processing a valid callback.

raw_findings.body: OAuthLoginView returns the generic invalid-state error before calling the installation API, so the test no longer verifies handling of GitHub's 404 response.

raw_findings.impact: OAuthLoginView returns the generic invalid-state error before calling the installation API, so the test no longer verifies handling of GitHub's 404 response.

raw_findings.failure_mode: The security regression test validates webhook authentication failure rather than installer/OAuth identity mismatch.
raw_findings.impact: The webhook is rejected or does not populate the integration with sender=attacker, so the test does not exercise the intended authenticated-user mismatch scenario.
raw_findings.root_cause: The test changes a signed event after importing it but leaves the original signature unchanged.

finding.title: User-mismatch test signs a different webhook payload than its HMAC
finding.trigger: Webhook signature verification is enabled when this test sends the mutated event body with the unchanged fixture signature.
finding.verifier_reason: Lines 417-423 show webhook payload modification (`sender.login = attacker`) after loading INSTALLATION_EVENT_EXAMPLE, but the signature at line 423 remains the original fixture's HMAC.
